title: Purple Blotch of Onion: How to Spot It and Stop It
metaTitle: Purple Blotch of Onion: Signs, Damage and Control
metaDescription: Purple blotch makes large brown to purple patches with rings on onion leaves and can rot the bulb neck. Learn the signs, causes and how to control it.
excerpt: Purple blotch is the fungal disease that makes large brown to purple patches, with rings, on onion leaves. It killed so much red onion in some Philippine areas in 2016 that planting was cut in half.

heroImage.alt: An onion family leaf with dark purple brown blotches from Alternaria porri
heroImage.credit: Landcare Research New Zealand, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text:
The fungus Alternaria porri causes purple blotch. It attacks onion, shallot, garlic and leek, and it occurs worldwide. The Pacific pest fact sheet notes that in 2016 the red onion area in parts of the Philippines fell to half. Purple blotch caused that drop.

The disease and the [thrips](/pests/thrips) go together. Older leaves that thrips have scarred are the easiest for the fungus to enter. Their feeding also helps the spread. So an onion grower should manage both together.

blocks.caption: Quick facts
rows: Leaves and fruits, pods and nuts
It builds in humid, wet weather and on older leaves, and it jumps when thrips have already scarred the leaves.
The fungus survives on crop debris, and spores move by wind, rain splash and possibly insects. The spores need about 8 hours of wet leaf to infect.

blocks.text: Look at the leaves and the flower stalk. Spots begin small and sunken with a white center. Then they grow quickly into oval, brown to purple blotches that can reach several centimeters. Pale and dark rings appear inside each blotch, like a target. When blotches circle the leaf, the part above them wilts, collapses and dies. At harvest, the bulb can rot from the neck, with a watery yellow to red decay.

items: Small, sunken spots with a white center appear on the leaves.
The spots grow into oval, brown to purple blotches, several centimeters long.
Light and dark rings show inside the blotches.
A blotch that circles the leaf makes the top wilt and die, and leaf tips turn black.
At harvest, the bulb neck rots, with a watery yellow to red decay.

blocks.title: Do not confuse it with
blocks.text: Purple blotch is easy to confuse with the scars left by [thrips](/pests/thrips). But only the disease makes large brown to purple blotches with light and dark rings.
How Purple Blotch Hurts Your Crop

Purple blotch can cause serious loss, mostly in the tropics. The Pacific pest fact sheet reports losses above 40 percent in Samoa. In 2016 the red onion area in parts of the Philippines fell to half. The loss comes from dead leaves, smaller bulbs and rot in storage.

I found no official action threshold for the Philippines. Humidity, long hours of leaf wetness and thrips damage all raise the risk. So the best time to act is before the first blotches. Our guide to [growing vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines) covers spacing and watering.

items: Use certified, disease free seed and sets, and plant healthy seedlings.
Check the nursery and remove any seedling that shows leaf spots before you transplant.
Use drip irrigation instead of overhead watering, so the leaves do not stay wet for long.
Control thrips. The fungus enters older leaves scarred by thrips, so see our page on [thrips](/pests/thrips).
Rotate for 3 years with crops outside the onion family, and bury or remove crop residue after harvest.
Check the bulb necks at harvest, since the fungus can infect the neck and cause a watery rot.

blocks.text: Onion growers where the disease is common use protectant sprays, along with systemic triazole fungicides. Mancozeb and chlorothalonil are the most common choices. Start protection before the disease builds, then rotate groups. Follow the FPA registered label for the rate and the waiting time before harvest.

blocks.title: Spray safely
blocks.text: Use only products registered with the [Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority](/blog/fertilizer-and-pesticide-authority), and follow the label for the rate, the timing and the protective clothing. Switch to a different fungicide group next time, so the disease does not learn to survive it. Our [guide to plant diseases](/diseases/plant-diseases-philippines) explains how.

items: Start each crop with clean seed or sets.
Rotate with other crops for 3 years.
Water by drip so the leaves do not stay wet.
Choose varieties that show resistance where they are sold, since resistance has been found in onion and garlic.

blocks.text: Questions Farmers Ask About Purple Blotch

items.q: What causes purple blotch on onion?
items.a: The fungus Alternaria porri causes it. Spores need about 8 hours of leaf wetness to infect, and thrips scars make it easier.

items.q: Can purple blotch rot the bulb?
items.a: Yes. The disease can infect the bulb at harvest, usually at the neck, where a watery yellow to red rot develops.

items.q: How do I keep it from coming back?
items.a: Rotate for 3 years, use clean seed, water by drip, control thrips and remove crop residue.
